% a tier 3 word, in English and in translation alike
\newcommand{\ealkey}[1]{\textcolor{ealkeycolour}{#1}}
\newcommand{\ealkeytr}[1]{\textcolor{ealkeycolour}{\ealtext{#1}}}

% One translated word above one English word. Built from kernel
% primitives, never a tabular, which would break wherever the sheet
% loads array, booktabs or tabularx. The box is as wide as the wider of
% the two, so a long translation pushes its neighbours aside instead of
% overlapping them, and it claims its full height so a table row or a
% TikZ node makes room for it.
\newcommand{\ealgloss}[2]{%
  \sbox{\ealboxen}{\ealkey{#1}}%
  \sbox{\ealboxtr}{\small\textcolor{ealtwocolour}{\ealtext{#2}}}%
  \setlength{\ealglosswd}{\wd\ealboxen}%
  \ifdim\wd\ealboxtr>\ealglosswd\setlength{\ealglosswd}{\wd\ealboxtr}\fi
  \leavevmode
  \makebox[\ealglosswd][c]{%
    \makebox[0pt][c]{\usebox{\ealboxen}}%
    \makebox[0pt][c]{\raisebox{\ealglossraise}{\usebox{\ealboxtr}}}%
  }%
}

% opens up line spacing around a block of glosses, so the raised
% translations sit clear of the line above
\newenvironment{ealglossed}{\par\linespread{2.1}\selectfont\ignorespaces}{\par}

% a whole translated sentence above its English counterpart. block level,
% so it does not belong inside a tabular cell
\newcommand{\ealpara}[2]{%
  \par\addvspace{0.5\baselineskip}%
  {\color{ealtwocolour}\ealtextblock{#1}}%
  \penalty200
  {\color{ealenglish}#2\par}%
  \addvspace{0.5\baselineskip}%
}

% ===============================================================
% PAGE 2 -- questions for part 1
% ===============================================================
\begin{center}
  {\LARGE\bfseries \ealpara{Część 1: pytania}{Part 1 questions}}
  \vspace{1.5mm}
  {\small \ealpara{Dla każdej osoby oblicz, które z sześciu \ealkeytr{kont} daje jej najwięcej pieniędzy, i ile będzie miała na końcu. Uważnie sprawdź warunki.}{For each person, work out which of the six \ealkey{accounts} gives them the most money, and how much they would have at the end. Check the conditions carefully.}}
\end{center}
\vspace{2mm}

\begin{qlist}
  \item \ealpara{\textbf{Amara} ma \pounds100 i chce zaoszczędzić je na \textbf{1 rok}.}{\textbf{Amara} has \pounds100 and wants to save it for \textbf{1 year}.}
  \item \ealpara{\textbf{Ben} ma \pounds200 i chce zaoszczędzić je na \textbf{2 lata}.}{\textbf{Ben} has \pounds200 and wants to save it for \textbf{2 years}.}
  \item \ealpara{\textbf{Chloe} ma \pounds400 i chce zaoszczędzić je na \textbf{4 lata}.}{\textbf{Chloe} has \pounds400 and wants to save it for \textbf{4 years}.}
  \item \ealpara{\textbf{Dev} ma \pounds1000 i chce zaoszczędzić je na \textbf{3 lata}.}{\textbf{Dev} has \pounds1000 and wants to save it for \textbf{3 years}.}
  \item \ealpara{\textbf{Erin} ma \pounds500 i chce zaoszczędzić je na \textbf{5 lat}.}{\textbf{Erin} has \pounds500 and wants to save it for \textbf{5 years}.}
  \item \ealpara{\textbf{Fay} ma \pounds250 do zaoszczędzenia na \textbf{3 lata}. Już zdecydowała, że użyje Coventree albo Starlight Bank. Który powinna wybrać i o ile będzie lepiej?}{\textbf{Fay} has \pounds250 to save for \textbf{3 years}. She has already decided to use either Coventree or Starlight Bank. Which should she choose, and how much better off will she be?}
\end{qlist}

\vfill
\ealpara{Pomyśl o tym}{Think about}
\begin{tcolorbox}[enhanced,colback=black!4,colframe=black!45,boxrule=0.8pt,arc=2mm,
                  left=4mm,right=4mm,top=3mm,bottom=3mm,
                  title={Think about},fonttitle=\bfseries,colbacktitle=black!45]
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=5mm,itemsep=2mm,topsep=1mm,label=\textbullet]
  \item \ealpara{Coventree i Starlight obie płacą 5\%. Wyjaśnij, dlaczego Starlight zawsze płaci co najmniej tyle samo co Coventree.}{Coventree and Starlight both pay 5\%. Explain why Starlight always pays at least as much as Coventree.}
  \item \ealpara{Ben mówi: „\ealkeytr{Konto} z największym \ealkeytr{procentem} zawsze jest najlepsze”. Czy ma rację? Użyj \ealkeytr{kont} z tej karty, aby wyjaśnić swoją odpowiedź.}{Ben says, ``The \ealkey{account} with the biggest \ealkey{percentage} is always the best one.'' Is he right? Use the \ealkey{accounts} on this sheet to explain your answer.}
\end{itemize}
\end{tcolorbox}

\vspace{4mm}
{\bfseries\large \ealpara{Pomyśl o tym}{Think about}}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=5mm,itemsep=2mm,topsep=2mm]
  \item \ealpara{\textbf{Coventree v Starlight.} Rok 1 jest identyczny: 5\% tej samej kwoty początkowej. Potem Starlight nalicza swoje 5\% od większego \ealkeytr{salda} co roku, więc nigdy nie może pozostać w tyle.}{\textbf{Coventree v Starlight.} Year 1 is identical: 5\% of the same starting amount. After that Starlight charges its 5\% on a larger \ealkey{balance} every year, so it can never fall behind.}
  \item \ealpara{\textbf{Największy \ealkeytr{procent}.} Nie. 10\% Metroline to najwyższa \ealkeytr{wielkość ilorazowa} w części 1, ale \ealkeytr{górny limit} \pounds300 czyni ją bezużyteczną dla Chloe, Dev i Erin.}{\textbf{Biggest \ealkey{percentage}.} No. Metroline's 10\% is the highest \ealkey{rate} in part 1, but the \pounds300 \ealkey{cap} makes it useless to Chloe, Dev and Erin.}
  \item \ealpara{\textbf{Trustbridge.} \ealkeytr{Wielkości ilorazowe} są proste, obliczane od pierwotnej \ealkeytr{wpłaty}, więc trzy lata dają 2\% + 4\% + 6\% = 12\% łącznie --- to daje \ealkeytr{średnią} tylko 4\% rocznie.}{\textbf{Trustbridge.} The \ealkey{rates} are simple, worked out on the original \ealkey{deposit}, so three years pays 2\% + 4\% + 6\% = 12\% in total --- only 4\% a year on \ealkey{average}.}
  \item \ealpara{\textbf{Nationworth.} Miesięczna \ealkeytr{opłata} \pounds2 kosztuje \pounds24 rocznie. Przy \pounds250 ta \ealkeytr{opłata} zjada więcej niż \ealkeytr{odsetki}; potrzebujesz ponad \pounds400 na \ealkeytr{koncie}, zanim 6\% w ogóle to pokryje.}{\textbf{Nationworth.} The \pounds2 monthly \ealkey{fee} costs \pounds24 a year. On \pounds250 that \ealkey{fee} wipes out more than the \ealkey{interest}; you need over \pounds400 in the \ealkey{account} before 6\% even covers it.}
  \item \ealpara{\textbf{Halifield.} Nie. Dwie porcje 2\% dają 1.02 $\times$ 1.02 = 1.0404, więc 4.04\% rocznie, trochę więcej niż 4\%.}{\textbf{Halifield.} No. Two lots of 2\% gives 1.02 $\times$ 1.02 = 1.0404, so 4.04\% a year, slightly more than 4\%.}
\end{itemize}
